questions.question: What is a quadratic form on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
options: A polynomial with at most two variables
Any polynomial with exactly two nonzero terms
A polynomial whose terms all have degree two
A polynomial that contains a constant term and a linear term

questions.question: Which matrix expression represents a quadratic form?
Which function is a quadratic form on $\mathbb{R}^2$?
Which term is allowed in a quadratic form in variables $x$ and $y$?
What is true about the associated matrix of a quadratic form?
options: It is always unique, even if it is not a symmetric matrix.
It is not unique, but there is a unique symmetric associated matrix
It cannot be symmetric unless the form is zero
It must be diagonal for every quadratic form

questions.question: Why is $x^2+2x+1$ not a quadratic form?
options: It contains terms that are not of degree two
It is written in one variable.
It can be represented by a matrix.

questions.question: For $f(x,y) = 3x^2+4xy+5y^2$, which matrix is a symmetric associated matrix?
Evaluate the quadratic form with symmetric matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&3\end{pmatrix}$ at $\boldsymbol{x} = (1,1)^\intercal$.
Why can two different matrices represent the same quadratic form?
options: The value of $\boldsymbol{x}$ is never used in the expression
Every matrix has the same entries after transposition
Quadratic forms do not depend on coefficients

questions.question: Which condition is essential for a polynomial to be a quadratic form rather than just a polynomial of degree $2$?
options: Every term must have degree exactly $2$
It must have exactly one square term
It must be written in exactly two variables
Its associated matrix must be diagonal

questions.question: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&5\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$. Which symmetric matrix gives the same quadratic form $\boldsymbol{x}^\intercal A\boldsymbol{x}$?
Which polynomial is degree $2$ but not a quadratic form?
What degrees do all terms in a quadratic form have?
Which expression has the standard quadratic-form shape?
What kind of term is $x_iy_j$ not allowed to be in a quadratic form on variables $x_1,\ldots,x_n$?
options: A term using a variable outside the chosen coordinate vector
A product of any two of the chosen coordinate variables.

questions.question: Which polynomial is a quadratic form?
Which degree-two term can appear in a quadratic form in $x$ and $y$?
For $f(x,y)=4x^2+6xy$, which statement is correct?
options: It cannot have a matrix representation.

questions.question: Why is the associated matrix of a quadratic form not unique?
options: Matrices with the same symmetric part give the same $\boldsymbol{x}^{\intercal}A\boldsymbol{x}$.
The matrix must always be diagonal.
The matrix must always be zero.
A quadratic form has no matrix expression whatsoever, in any form.
